title: Population of England before the census, competing estimates
label: Broadberry, Campbell & van Leeuwen 2011
note: Historians disagree most about the peak before the Black Death: from about 3.7 million (Russell) to about 6 million (Postan, Clark). Broadberry, Campbell and van Leeuwen's series (1086–1541) is built from manorial and tax records; Wrigley and colleagues' (1541–1801, England without Monmouthshire) from parish registers. Dots are other published estimates, with their ranges; hover for whose each is. The censuses begin in 1801.

title: Population at each census

title: Population

title: Population of Ireland before the census, competing estimates
label: Connell 1950
note: Before the first full census of 1821 Ireland's population is estimated from hearth-tax returns, which scholars correct in different ways: Connell's figures are higher than Daultrey, Dickson and Ó Gráda's (shown with their ranges). Dots are other estimates, from medieval guesses to contemporary counts such as Petty's of 1672. All are for the whole island; the census graph for Ireland covers the 26 counties of the State.

title: Population at each census

title: Tea retained for home consumption
unit_long: million pounds of tea retained for home consumption a year
label: Tea retained for home consumption (Statistical Abstract)
note: The whole quantity of tea retained for home consumption: in the Abstract's words, found "by deducting the Quantities Over-Entered, and those Exported subsequently to the payment of the Duties, from the Quantities Entered for Home Consumption in the first instance", from the Board of Trade's earliest Statistical Abstracts, 1846-1865. Ireland included. Editions Nos. 8 and 13 read from the page images; the overlapping years (1851-1860) agree. The quantity doubled in those twenty years (46.7 million lb in 1846, 97.8 million in 1865).

title: Tea drunk per person
unit_long: pounds of tea retained for home consumption per person a year
label: Tea per head (Statistical Abstract)
note: Tea retained for home consumption (imports less re-exports) divided by the whole population, as printed by the Board of Trade; the first per-head table (No. 14, covering 1852-1866) starts in 1852. Ireland is included to 1922; from 1923 the figures are for Great Britain and Northern Ireland. None given for 1915-18. While the tea duty was repealed (1929-32) the figures are retained imports and not strictly comparable. Editions revised earlier years slightly (by up to 0.03 lb) after each census; the latest edition read is used. From 1941 the Ministry of Food's (later MAFF's) estimated supplies per head are shown as a second line: a different measure (supplies moving into consumption; per head of the civilian population to 1947), which gives 9.3 lb for 1934-38 against 9.5 here. The Abstracts read give no figures for 1939-40.

title: Tea supplies per person
unit_long: pounds of tea per person a year (estimated supplies)
label: Tea supplies per head (Ministry of Food / MAFF)
note: Estimated supplies of tea moving into consumption per head of population, from the Ministry of Food (the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food in the 1960 and later editions), as printed in the Annual Abstract of Statistics. Per head of the civilian population 1941-47; 1964-74 revised to the 1971 census. Editions revised single years by 0.1-0.2 lb; the latest edition read is used.
